amendments.body: PlantPreset and SubstratePreset do not implement param_meta support. The acceptance criteria states the schema should be 'flexible enough for both chemistry and biology parameters.' The ParamMeta schema itself is flexible, but plant parameters like growth_rate_index and water_column_uptake_bias — which are biology-relevant scientific parameters — cannot carry provenance at the preset level. Consider adding param_meta to PlantPreset (at minimum) for consistency, since the next bead (tanksim-6e5.7.2: 'Attach provenance to high-value chemistry and ecology parameters') will need to annotate plant params.
amendments.rationale: PlantPreset is a biology-relevant preset type with tunable scientific parameters. Without param_meta support, the downstream bead will need to add it as a prerequisite, which could have been done now alongside the other three preset types.

amendments.body: The acceptance criteria requires 'Decide how provenance is stored for code-defined defaults versus data-file parameters.' The implementation correctly uses TOML-level provenance for data-file params, and ProcessParams::Default has no inline provenance. However, this design decision is not documented anywhere — there is no comment in provenance.rs, process.rs, or the TOML files explicitly stating that code-defined defaults inherit provenance only when loaded through a TOML preset file, and that ProcessParams::Default values constructed without TOML have no provenance path. Add a brief design note (e.g., in provenance.rs or ROUTING.md) so downstream contributors understand the provenance boundary.
amendments.rationale: The decision was made implicitly by not adding provenance to ProcessParams::Default. Making it explicit prevents future contributors from wondering whether code defaults should carry inline provenance, and documents the boundary for the next bead.

payload.summary: The provenance schema and loader support implementation is solid, well-structured, and meets all six acceptance criteria. The core schema (ParamMeta, ConfidenceLevel in provenance.rs) is cleanly separated from integration (ParamMetaPreset trait in presets.rs) and loader support (diagnostic-aware loaders in lib.rs). Key design strengths: `deny_unknown_fields` on ParamMeta catches TOML typos at deser time; unknown param_meta keys are caught during validate(); legacy `_mg` parameters are correctly normalized to concentration units for range checks; out-of-range values produce warnings not errors; backward compatibility is maintained via serde defaults. All 22 tank_data tests and 11 provenance unit tests pass. No correctness bugs or safety issues found in the provenance-specific code.
